title: What to watch at the open
text: Monday was rough for tech. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ fell 1.4% to $681.09 and the S&P 500 fund SPY fell 0.5% to $752.10. Tech companies on the Nasdaq dropped about 3.5% on average, while makers of everyday products rose about 2.4%. At the open, watch whether the chip stocks keep falling or settle down, and remember AMD reports its results after the market closes today. One quiet morning does not mean the worry is gone. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Tech had a big down day
text: AMD fell 7.5% to $466.84, Vertiv fell 3.6% to $224.24, Rocket Lab fell 4.9% to $52.07 and Microsoft fell 2.8% to $507.12. These companies are tied to AI and fast growth, so they often move together, up or down.

title: AMD reports after the close today
text: AMD said it will share its third quarter results today, Tuesday, after the market closes. The company told investors to expect about $13 billion in sales, and analysts expect a similar number. The price can jump or drop based on how the results compare with what people hoped for, so the move can happen tomorrow morning.

title: Long term interest rates eased a little
text: The 10 year Treasury yield, the interest the government pays to borrow for ten years, was 4.91% on Monday. That is down from 5.05% on October 28. The monthly average for October was 5.13%, the highest in our 12 month chart. Higher rates make safer investments more attractive, which can weigh on growth stocks.

title: GE and Amazon rose on a down day
text: GE Aerospace rose 4.6% to $315.78 and Amazon rose 2.2% to $245.63, while Lockheed Martin edged up 1.0% to $643.15. Our data does not say why. It shows that on the same day, different industries can move in opposite directions.

title: Lesson 34: Market orders and limit orders
text: When you buy a stock, you choose how to place the order. A market order says, buy now at whatever price is available. It is fast, but the price can be a little different from the one you saw, especially in the first minutes after the market opens when prices jump around. A limit order says, buy only at this price or better. You set the price, but the order may never happen if the stock does not reach it. Neither one is better for everyone. Many people who are learning like limit orders because they teach patience and show exactly what you agreed to pay. This is education, not advice.
